s: On which date did the Nizam and the Government of India sign the Standstill Agreement?
x:
The Standstill Agreement between the Government of India and the Nizam of Hyderabad was signed on 29 November 1947. The agreement was intended to maintain the existing administrative, economic and communication arrangements between Hyderabad State and the Dominion of India for one year while negotiations regarding Hyderabad's future continued. However, the Nizam continued efforts to remain independent, leading to increasing political unrest. The issue was finally resolved through Operation Polo (Police Action) in September 1948, resulting in the integration of Hyderabad into the Indian Union. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).
Exam Note:
• Standstill Agreement – 29 November 1947
• Parties – Government of India & Nizam of Hyderabad

s: When did the Hyderabad Police Action come to an end?
x:
Operation Polo, popularly known as the Hyderabad Police Action, was launched by the Government of India on 13 September 1948 to integrate Hyderabad State into the Indian Union. The Hyderabad State Forces, commanded by Major General El Edroos, surrendered on 17 September 1948, bringing the operation to an end. Hyderabad thereafter became part of the Indian Union. Hence, the correct answer is Option (2).

• Operation Polo → 13–17 September 1948
• Hyderabad integrated into the Indian Union → 17 September 1948

After five days of fighting, El Edroos surrendered on 17 September 1948, resulting in the integration of Hyderabad State into the Indian Union. Hence, the correct answer is Option (3).

x: After the Quit India Movement in 1942, India faced a significant political and constitutional deadlock between the British government, the Indian National Congress, and the Muslim League, primarily over the issue of Indian independence and the demand for Pakistan. C. Rajagopalachari (CR) issued his pamphlet "The Way Out" in 1944 to propose a formula (known as the C.R. Formula) to resolve this impasse and facilitate Congress-League cooperation. The C.R. s: "It made its proposals in May. It still wanted a united India. There was to be a Federal Union composed of British provinces." The above quotation is related to:
x: The quotation refers to the Cabinet Mission Plan of May 1946, published on 16 May. It aimed to preserve Indian unity while addressing communal divisions through a federal scheme. The Plan proposed a three-tier federation with a central authority limited to defence, foreign affairs, and communications, and provinces grouped into regional clusters—thus forming a Federal Union of British provinces.
